subject: SIG: Access controls — SAML/SCIM/RBAC/MFA matrix and follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Royce <alex.royce@acme-corp.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: megan.lin@acme-corp.com
Date: 2025-11-04T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SIG: Access controls — quick clarification and evidence ask

Markus,

Thanks for the SIG intake so far. A couple of follow-ups from our InfoSec team specific to access controls (we're consolidating SIG-L and SIG-A items):

- SCIM: how do you handle deprovisioning? Do you send Delta operations or full replace? For deleted users do you soft-delete/suspend in Redwood or immediately remove access?
- RBAC: we need a role inventory CSV and a brief mapping to least-privilege guidance (e.g., which roles can create API keys, which roles can view billing).
- SSO/SAML: please provide SAML metadata (IdP/SP details) and confirm support for both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. Any attribute mappings (NameID/email, groups) would be helpful.
- MFA: confirm whether Redwood enforces MFA centrally or relies on IdP MFA; what about service accounts/API keys?

Can you send the artifacts and short answers by EOD Nov 7? We want to close this tranche of SIG questions and move to evidence review.

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Royce
Security Lead, Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com

From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Royce <alex.royce@acme-corp.com>
Cc: megan.lin@acme-corp.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-05T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Access controls — quick clarification and evidence ask

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. High-level answers up front, attachments & deeper details to follow from Karthik and Stephanie:

- SCIM: push-based SCIM 2.0 with incremental (PATCH) support; deprovisioning is configurable per-customer (we support immediate disable + soft-delete retention window configurable 0–30 days). See attached scim-schema.csv for attribute list and deprovisioning options.
- RBAC: attached rbac-role-inventory.csv (columns: role_id, role_name, permissions, recommended_practice). Default roles: Viewer, Developer, Model-Operator, Admin, Billing. Only Admin and Billing can manage invoices/credits; API key creation is scoped to Developer+ above by default but can be restricted.
- SAML: we support SAML 2.0 SP with both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows; metadata export attached (saml-config-export.xml) with ACS/EntityID placeholders. Group-to-role mapping is supported via SAML attribute or via SCIM group sync.
- MFA: we enforce MFA for interactive console access for all Redwood accounts; for SSO customers we rely on IdP-enforced MFA for the SSO path. Service accounts/API keys do not enforce MFA (not interactive), but we provide short-lived tokens, key rotation tooling, and token-scoped restrictions (IP, route-level perms). See attached mfa-policy.pdf for policy & recommended controls.

I'll hand Karthik the SCIM and SAML technical follow-ups and Stephanie the RBAC/least-privilege justification. We should be able to produce a consolidated PDF by Nov 10.

Action items:
- Karthik: provide attribute mapping examples and delta vs full behavior details.
- Stephanie: annotate role inventory with least-privilege mapping and suggested hardening steps.

Markus
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: saml-config-export.xml, scim-schema.csv, rbac-role-inventory.csv, mfa-policy.pdf

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Royce <alex.royce@acme-corp.com>, megan.lin@acme-corp.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-07T11:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Access controls — SCIM/SAML technical details

Alex / Megan — deep diving into the SCIM and SAML behavior per Markus' note. Short technical answers you can paste into SIG fields: 

SCIM provisioning (behavior):
- Protocol: SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7643/7644).
- Operations: support for POST (create), PUT (replace), PATCH (incremental updates), DELETE.
- Deprovisioning: by default we send DELETE for user removal; we also offer a 'suspend' workflow where SCIM sends "active":false and Redwood marks the user as suspended (no console access, tokens revoked) and retains the record for configurable retention window (default 14 days). Customers can opt to invert behavior to soft-delete only (i.e., mark inactive).
- Group sync: we support group membership push; group exclusions are supported using a filter list (excludeGroups parameter) at provisioning configuration.

SAML attributes & flows:
- SAML standard: 2.0 (SP-initiated + IdP-initiated).
- NameID: we recommend email (transient or persistent as agreed).
- Attributes: urn:oid:1.3.6.1.4.1.5923.1.1.1.1 (eduPersonPrincipalName) OR email, plus groups attribute (urn:oid:2.5.4.11 or 'groups').
- Group-to-role mapping: supported via SAML attribute mapping or by SCIM group sync. If both are present, SCIM wins for authoritative membership.

Session & token invalidation:
- Suspension path: when a user is suspended (active=false), we immediately mark the account suspended and revoke all active refresh tokens and session cookies. Access tokens are short-lived (1h); revocation is best-effort for in-flight tokens but subsequent API calls will fail.
- Deletion path: DELETE will remove the account and all associated tokens; audit record retained per customer retention setting.

Example SCIM PATCH to suspend a user (RFC 7644):
PATCH /scim/v2/Users/2819-2819
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [{
    "op": "replace",
    "path": "active",
    "value": false
  }]
}

Let me know if you want a sample SCIM connector config for Okta/JumpCloud — I can attach one.

-Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Identity
Redwood Inference

From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Royce <alex.royce@acme-corp.com>, megan.lin@acme-corp.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-09T09:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Access controls — RBAC & least-privilege mapping

Hi Alex / Megan — attaching our role inventory (rbac-role-inventory.csv) with annotations. Highlights you can include in SIG narrative:

- Least-privilege default: customers are onboarded with principle of least privilege via a minimal default role (Viewer) and scoped opt-in for higher privilege.
- Role examples:
  - Viewer: read-only access to logs, model outputs, and metrics.
  - Developer: create/delete model routes, generate API keys (can be restricted).
  - Model-Operator: manage serving pools, rollouts (no billing access).
  - Admin: tenant-level config, user management.
  - Billing: view invoices, request credits.

- Hardening recommendations: restrict API key creation to a service account role, enable IP whitelisting, require periodic key rotation (we surface rotation reminders).
- Evidence: rbac-role-inventory.csv (attached) + sample audit log snippets are available on request.

If you want, we can produce a CSV that directly maps SIG control IDs (e.g., SIG-AC-07) to our evidence filenames.

-Stephanie
Security PM, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: SIG access controls packet (consolidated)

Alex / Megan — thanks for the back-and-forth. Attached is a consolidated package (redwood-sig-responses-2025-11-10.pdf) that contains the finalized answers for the SIG access-controls section and the raw artifacts we referenced (SAML metadata, SCIM attribute list, RBAC inventory, MFA policy).

Key points called out in the doc:
- SCIM: 2.0, supports PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE. Deprovisioning is configurable; suspension immediately revokes sessions/tokens.
- SAML: 2.0 SP supports both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows; group attribute + NameID mappings documented.
- RBAC: default least-privilege onboarding; role inventory included with explicit permissions for high-risk actions (billing, key creation, role management).
- MFA & service accounts: interactive users must use MFA (IdP-enforced for SSO); API keys are short-lived or rotated and can be constrained by IP and route.

Next steps if you need more evidence: we can provide audit log extracts for a limited timebox, a sample Okta SCIM connector config, or a video demo of role mapping.

Would you like us to upload the final package to your secure intake bucket? If yes, we can push to the HubSpot deal folder and send the DocuSign (if you prefer an acceptance signature).

Thanks — Markus
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
